stem_text: A block of mass m, lying on a smooth horizontal surface, is attached to a spring (of negligible mass) of spring constant k. The other end of the spring is fixed, as shown in the figure. The block is initially at rest in its equilibrium position. If now the block is pulled with a constant force F, the maximum speed of the block is : [FIG-stem-1]
figure_reference: [FIG-stem-1] Horizontal spring-block setup unverified against master

candidate_solve.derivation: Maximum speed occurs at the equilibrium position where net force is zero: F_net = F - k*x = 0 => x_0 = F/k. By Work-Energy Theorem from rest (x=0, v=0) to equilibrium position (x_0, v_max): W_net = W_force + W_spring = Delta KE => F*x_0 - 1/2 k x_0^2 = 1/2 m v_max^2. Substituting x_0 = F/k: F*(F/k) - 1/2 k*(F/k)^2 = F^2/k - F^2/(2k) = F^2/(2k) = 1/2 m v_max^2 => v_max^2 = F^2 / (mk) => v_max = F / sqrt(mk). Matches Option D.
candidate_solve.limiting_cases: If k -> infinity, v_max -> 0. If m -> infinity, v_max -> 0. Simple harmonic motion verification: equilibrium shift x_0 = F/k, amplitude A = F/k, angular frequency omega = sqrt(k/m), maximum speed v_max = omega * A = sqrt(k/m) * (F/k) = F / sqrt(mk).
